NHWA Module 1 (stock and flow) extension data elements, at a glance
ind:nhwa-1-01:
Indicator. 1-01 Health worker density

NHWA indicator 1-01: Health worker density. Density of health workers per 10 000 population

Numerator Denominator Disaggregation
Number of active health workers, defined in headcounts Total population By occupation, by occupation and activity level

Definition: Number of health workers per 10 000 population. For activity level the following categories are recommended: practising health workers, professionally active health workers, and health workers licensed to practise. Total population as estimated in the World Population Prospects published by the Population Division of the Department of Economic and Social Affairs of the United Nations Secretariat. In case of other methodology used, WHO recalculates densities according to the UN population estimates in order to harmonize the densities and ensure comparability.

Potential data sources: Health workforce registry or database; Aggregate data from health facilities (routine administrative records, Health Management Information System, District Health Information System census and/or survey); Professional council/chamber/association registers; Labour force surveys; Population census data; United Nations Population Division.

Reporting: Annual. Frameworks: UN SDG 3.c.1, SDG 3.8.1, WHO Global Code of Practice on the International Recruitment of Health Personnel, Global Strategy for Human Resources for Health: Workforce 2030 (GSHRH), Working for Health programme, Global Strategic Directions for Nursing and Midwifery (SDNM), Immunization Agenda 2030 (IA2030), SCORE for Health Data Technical Package (SCORE), Primary Health Care (PHC) Measurement Framework, Community Health Workers (CHWs), Global Oral Health Action Plan.

Data elements in this chapter: de:cde-occupation, de:cde-employment-status, de:nhwa-m1-activity-level, de:cde-professional-licence-and-certification.

Source: National health workforce accounts: a handbook, 2nd edition, indicator 1-01 (page 52), word for word, from the ingested L1 node in who-iris. Draft L2 indicator NHWA.1-01, for working-group review.
ind:nhwa-1-02:
Indicator. 1-02 Health worker density at subnational level

NHWA indicator 1-02: Health worker density at subnational level. Density of active health workers per 10 000 population at subnational level

Numerator Denominator Disaggregation
Number of active health workers in level 1 subnational administrative units Total population at subnational level By occupation

Definition: Number of active health workers per 10 000 population in the given subnational administrative unit. Preferably, the subnational unit should correspond to the place of work of health workers. The use of administrative units to the first subnational level is recommended (depending on the structure of administrative units and the size of subnational territories), without overlaps between the administrative units. Examples of subnational administrative units include states, regions, provinces, counties, and districts.

Potential data sources: Health workforce registry or database; Aggregate data from health facilities (routine administrative records, Health Management Information System, District Health Information System census and/or survey); Professional council/chamber/association registers; Population census data; Health facility database (with location); United Nations Population Division.

Reporting: Annual. Frameworks: UN SDG 3.c.1, Global Strategy for Human Resources for Health: Workforce 2030 (GSHRH), Working for Health programme, Global Strategic Directions for Nursing and Midwifery (SDNM), SCORE for Health Data Technical Package (SCORE), Primary Health Care (PHC) Measurement Framework.

Data elements in this chapter: de:cde-occupation, de:cde-employment-address, de:nhwa-m1-subnational-unit.

Source: National health workforce accounts: a handbook, 2nd edition, indicator 1-02 (page 53), word for word, from the ingested L1 node in who-iris. Draft L2 indicator NHWA.1-02, for working-group review.
ind:nhwa-1-03:
Indicator. 1-03 Health worker distribution by age group

NHWA indicator 1-03: Health worker distribution by age group. Percentage of active health workers in different age groups

Numerator Denominator Disaggregation
Number of active health workers in age group categories Total number of active health workers, defined in headcounts By occupation, by occupation and sex

Definition: Percentage of active health workers in the given age and sex category. This indicator enables to create the population pyramid of health workers. Age groups considered are the following: < 25, 25–34, 35–44, 45–54, 55–64, ≥ 65 years. Sex groups corresponds to male or female health workers.

Potential data sources: Health workforce registry or database; Aggregate data from health facilities (routine administrative records, Health Management Information System, District Health Information System census and/or survey); Professional council/chamber/association registers; Labour force surveys; Population census data.

Reporting: Annual. Frameworks: UN SDG 3.c.1, Global Strategic Directions for Nursing and Midwifery (SDNM), SCORE for Health Data Technical Package (SCORE).

Data elements in this chapter: de:cde-birth-history, de:cde-occupation, de:cde-sex.

Source: National health workforce accounts: a handbook, 2nd edition, indicator 1-03 (page 54), word for word, from the ingested L1 node in who-iris. Draft L2 indicator NHWA.1-03, for working-group review.
ind:nhwa-1-04:
Indicator. 1-04 Health worker distribution by sex

NHWA indicator 1-04: Health worker distribution by sex. Percentage of active health workers by sex

Numerator Denominator Disaggregation
Number of active health workers in sex categories Total number of active male and female health workers, defined in headcounts By occupation

Definition: Percentage of active health workers in the given sex category. Sex group corresponds to male or female health workers.

Potential data sources: Health workforce registry or database; Aggregate data from health facilities (routine administrative records, Health Management Information System, District Health Information System census and/or survey); Labour force surveys; Population census data.

Reporting: Annual. Frameworks: UN SDG 3.c.1, Global Strategic Directions for Nursing and Midwifery (SDNM), SCORE for Health Data Technical Package (SCORE).

Data elements in this chapter: de:cde-occupation, de:cde-sex.

Source: National health workforce accounts: a handbook, 2nd edition, indicator 1-04 (page 55), word for word, from the ingested L1 node in who-iris. Draft L2 indicator NHWA.1-04, for working-group review.
ind:nhwa-1-05:
Indicator. 1-05 Health worker distribution by facility ownership

NHWA indicator 1-05: Health worker distribution by facility ownership. Percentage of active health workers employed by facility ownership

Numerator Denominator Disaggregation
Number of active health workers, defined in headcounts, working in facilities owned by the given institutional sector (public or private not-for-profit or private for-profit) Total number of active health workers, defined in headcounts By occupation

Definition: Percentage of active health workers employed by facility ownership (public, private not-for-profit, private for-profit). The categories of facility ownership can be aligned to institutional sector definitions of the System of National Accounts (SNA 2008).

Potential data sources: Health workforce registry or database; Aggregate data from health facilities (routine administrative records, Health Management Information System, District Health Information System census and/or survey); Labour force surveys; Census.

Reporting: Annual. Frameworks: SCORE for Health Data Technical Package (SCORE).

Data elements in this chapter: de:cde-occupation, de:cde-employment-address, de:nhwa-m1-facility-ownership.

Source: National health workforce accounts: a handbook, 2nd edition, indicator 1-05 (page 56), word for word, from the ingested L1 node in who-iris. Draft L2 indicator NHWA.1-05, for working-group review.
ind:nhwa-1-06:
Indicator. 1-06 Health worker distribution by facility type

NHWA indicator 1-06: Health worker distribution by facility type. Percentage of active health workers employed by facility type

Numerator Denominator Disaggregation
Number of active health workers, defined in headcounts, working in a specific facility type Total number of active health workers, defined in headcounts By occupation

Definition: Percentage of active health workers employed in the given facility type. Health facility types are based on the classification of System of Health Accounts: • Hospitals (HP.1) • Residential long-term care facilities (HP.2) • Providers of ambulatory health care (HP.3) • Ancillary services (HP.4, including transportation, emergency rescue, laboratories and others) • Retailers (HP.5, including pharmacies) • Providers of preventive care (HP.6)

Potential data sources: Health workforce registry or database; Aggregate data from health facilities (routine administrative records, Health Management Information System, District Health Information System census and/or survey); Labour Force Surveys; Census.

Reporting: Annual.

Data elements in this chapter: de:cde-occupation, de:cde-employment-address, de:nhwa-m1-facility-type.

Source: National health workforce accounts: a handbook, 2nd edition, indicator 1-06 (page 57), word for word, from the ingested L1 node in who-iris. Draft L2 indicator NHWA.1-06, for working-group review.
ind:nhwa-1-07:
Indicator. 1-07 Health worker distribution by place of birth

NHWA indicator 1-07: Health worker distribution by place of birth. Percentage of active health workers by their place of birth

Numerator Denominator Disaggregation
Number of active health workers by place of birth Total number of active health workers, defined in headcounts By occupation

Definition: Percentage of active health workers by their place of birth. Place of birth is defined as national-born or foreign-born. This indicator will capture the information on the health workers coming from abroad.

Potential data sources: Health workforce registry or database; Professional council/chamber/association registers; Health facility data; Population census data.

Reporting: Annual. Frameworks: WHO Global Code of Practice on the International Recruitment of Health Personnel, Global Strategic Directions for Nursing and Midwifery (SDNM).

Data elements in this chapter: de:cde-birth-history, de:cde-occupation, de:cde-citizenship-and-language.

Source: National health workforce accounts: a handbook, 2nd edition, indicator 1-07 (page 58), word for word, from the ingested L1 node in who-iris. Draft L2 indicator NHWA.1-07, for working-group review.
ind:nhwa-1-08:
Indicator. 1-08 Health worker distribution by place of training

NHWA indicator 1-08: Health worker distribution by place of training. Percentage of active health workers by their place of training

Numerator Denominator Disaggregation
Number of active health workers by place of training Total number of active health workers, defined in headcounts By occupation, by occupation and country of training among foreign-trained, by occupation and place of birth among foreign-trained

Definition: Percentage of active health workers by their place of training. Place of training is defined as either domestic-trained, foreign-trained or unknown location of training. The disaggregation by occupation and country of training is applicable to foreign-trained workers, and enables the monitoring of health worker migration by country of training. The disaggregation by occupation and place of birth is applicable to foreign-trained workers, and enables the monitoring of foreign-trained – national-born and foreign-trained – foreign-born workers.

Potential data sources: Health workforce registry or database; Professional council/chamber/association registers; Health facility data.

Reporting: Annual. Frameworks: WHO Global Code of Practice on the International Recruitment of Health Personnel, Global Strategy for Human Resources for Health: Workforce 2030 (GSHRH), Global Strategic Directions for Nursing and Midwifery (SDNM).

Data elements in this chapter: de:cde-occupation, de:nhwa-m1-place-of-training.

Source: National health workforce accounts: a handbook, 2nd edition, indicator 1-08 (page 59), word for word, from the ingested L1 node in who-iris. Draft L2 indicator NHWA.1-08, for working-group review.
ind:nhwa-1-09:
Indicator. 1-09 Annual inflows of health workers

NHWA indicator 1-09: Annual inflows of health workers. Ratio of newly active health workers to the total stock of active health workers

Numerator Denominator Disaggregation
Number of newly active health workers Total number of active health workers, defined in headcounts By occupation, by occupation and place of training, by occupation, place of training and sex

Definition: Newly active health workers are those who started their activity in the given profession. In case data are available only for newly licensed health workers, the total number of licensed health workers should be used as denominator regardless of availability of data on active health workers. For total number of active health workers, data at the middle or the end of the reference year should be used. Disaggregation by place of training (domestic-trained vs foreign-trained) enables to capture the health labour market dynamics of migration.

Potential data sources: Ministry of Health database; Health workforce registry or database; Professional council/chamber/association registers; Aggregate data from health facilities (routine administrative records, Health Management Information System, District Health Information System census and/or survey).

Reporting: Annual. Frameworks: Global Strategic Directions for Nursing and Midwifery (SDNM), SCORE for Health Data Technical Package (SCORE).

Data elements in this chapter: de:cde-occupation, de:cde-sex, de:cde-employment-status, de:nhwa-m1-entry-date, de:nhwa-m1-place-of-training.

Source: National health workforce accounts: a handbook, 2nd edition, indicator 1-09 (page 60), word for word, from the ingested L1 node in who-iris. Draft L2 indicator NHWA.1-09, for working-group review.
ind:nhwa-1-10:
Indicator. 1-10 Annual outflows of health workers

NHWA indicator 1-10: Annual outflows of health workers. Ratio of active health workers leaving the health labour market to the total stock of active health workers

Numerator Denominator Disaggregation
Number of health workers who became inactive in the health labour market Total number of active health workers, defined in headcounts By occupation, by occupation and type of exit (voluntary vs involuntary), by occupation, type of exit and sex

Definition: Percentage of active health workers who became inactive in the health labour market due to voluntary reason or involuntary reason The disaggregation by type of exit has the following two categories: • Voluntary exit corresponds to the following situations: emigration, temporary leave, change of sector, early retirement or other voluntary reason. Only early retirement should be considered as voluntary exit; retirement at standard age is to be counted in the involuntary exit. • Involuntary exit corresponds to the following situations: death, retirement (excluding early retirement), suspension from work, long-term illness or other involuntary reason. For the total number of active health workers, data at the end of the previous year should be used.

Potential data sources: Health workforce registry or database; Professional council/chamber/association registers; Aggregate data from health facilities (routine administrative records, Health Management Information System, District Health Information System census and/or survey); Data from pension and/or retirement administration units; Mortality records.

Reporting: Annual. Frameworks: SCORE for Health Data Technical Package (SCORE).

Data elements in this chapter: de:cde-occupation, de:cde-sex, de:cde-employment-status, de:nhwa-m1-exit.

Source: National health workforce accounts: a handbook, 2nd edition, indicator 1-10 (page 61), word for word, from the ingested L1 node in who-iris. Draft L2 indicator NHWA.1-10, for working-group review.
ind:nhwa-1-11:
Indicator. 1-11 Vacancy rate

NHWA indicator 1-11: Vacancy rate. Ratio of unfilled posts to total number of funded posts

Numerator Denominator Disaggregation
Number of funded full-time posts that have not been filled for at least twelve months Total number of funded full-time posts (filled and unfilled) By occupation

Definition: Ratio of unfilled posts to total number of posts. By limiting the count of unfilled posts for at least twelve months, this indicator enables to distinguish between a systematic job vacancy situation versus potential rapid turnover of staff.

Potential data sources: Labour force surveys; Health facility assessments; Employment offices and/or job agencies.

Reporting: Annual. Frameworks: Global Strategic Directions for Nursing and Midwifery (SDNM), SCORE for Health Data Technical Package (SCORE).

Source: National health workforce accounts: a handbook, 2nd edition, indicator 1-11 (page 62), word for word, from the ingested L1 node in who-iris. Draft L2 indicator NHWA.1-11, for working-group review.
ind:nhwa-1-12:
Indicator. 1-12 Health worker distribution by type of contract

NHWA indicator 1-12: Health worker distribution by type of contract. Percentage of active health workers by their type of contract

Numerator Denominator Disaggregation
Number of active health workers in specific types of contracts (full-time vs part-time) Total number of active health workers, defined in headcounts By occupation

Definition: Percentage of active health workers in the given type of contract. Type of contract are defined as either full-time or part-time. • Full-time workers are defined as employed or self-employed persons whose normal working hours in their main job correspond at least to the legal number of working hours per week, i.e. usually working 30 hours per week or above. • Part-time workers are defined as employed or self-employed persons whose normal hours of work are less than those of comparable full-time workers.

Potential data sources: Facility database and/or surveys; Health workforce registry or database; Labour force surveys; Public service human resources and payroll administrations.

Reporting: Annual.

Data elements in this chapter: de:cde-occupation, de:nhwa-m1-type-of-contract.

Source: National health workforce accounts: a handbook, 2nd edition, indicator 1-12 (page 63), word for word, from the ingested L1 node in who-iris. Draft L2 indicator NHWA.1-12, for working-group review.

prose:ch11-nhwa-m2:
• Extension data elements a registry needs to report NHWA Module 2 (education).
  • Of the module's indicators, 2-04 (ratio of graduates to stock) names a health workforce registry or database as a data source.
  • Indicators 2-01 to 2-03 and 2-05 to 2-07 describe education places, applications and programmes, and come from ministries of education and training institutions.

Table.

# Data element NHWA indicators Categories (NHWA handbook) Definition
1 Qualification and education programme 2-04 — to draft
2 Training institution and year of graduation 2-04 — to draft

NHWA Module 2 (education) extension data elements, at a glance
ind:nhwa-2-01:
Indicator. 2-01 Health workforce education and training capacity

NHWA indicator 2-01: Health workforce education and training capacity. Ratio of health workforce education and training capacity per 10 000 population

Numerator Denominator Disaggregation
Number of places in health education and training institutions Total population By health workforce education and training programme

Definition: The health workforce education and training capacity refers to the number of places or seats. This indicator enables to estimate the availability of the training capacity and express it per 10 000 population. Total population as estimated in the World Population Prospects by the United Nations Population Division. In case of other methodology used, WHO recalculates densities according to the UN population estimates in order to harmonize the densities and ensure comparability.

Potential data sources: Ministry of Education; Data on education and training statistics; Education and training institutions; United Nations Population Division.

Reporting: Annual.

Source: National health workforce accounts: a handbook, 2nd edition, indicator 2-01 (page 66), word for word, from the ingested L1 node in who-iris. Draft L2 indicator NHWA.2-01, for working-group review.
ind:nhwa-2-02:
Indicator. 2-02 Ratio of applications to education and training capacity

NHWA indicator 2-02: Ratio of applications to education and training capacity. Ratio of applications for health workforce education and training to the training capacity

Numerator Denominator Disaggregation
Number of applications for the first year of a health workforce education and training programme Total number of places available in the first year of a health workforce education and training programme By health workforce education and training programme, by health workforce education and training programme and sex

Definition: Applications for the first year of a health workforce education and training programme divided by the number of training places for this first year.

Potential data sources: Ministry of Education; Ministry of Higher Education; Databases on education and training statistics; education and training institutions.

Reporting: Annual. Frameworks: Global Strategic Directions for Nursing and Midwifery (SDNM).

Source: National health workforce accounts: a handbook, 2nd edition, indicator 2-02 (page 67), word for word, from the ingested L1 node in who-iris. Draft L2 indicator NHWA.2-02, for working-group review.
ind:nhwa-2-03:
Indicator. 2-03 Ratio of enrolments to application

NHWA indicator 2-03: Ratio of enrolments to application. Ratio of students enrolled in the first year of health workforce education and training programmes to applications for these programmes

Numerator Denominator Disaggregation
Total number of enrolments in the first year of a health workforce education and training programme Total number of applications for the first year of a health workforce education and training programme By health workforce education and training programme, by health workforce education and training programme and sex

Definition: Ratio of enrolment in health workforce education and training programmes to applications.

Potential data sources: Databases on education statistics; Education and training institutions.

Reporting: Annual. Frameworks: Global Strategy for Human Resources for Health: Workforce 2030 (GSHRH), Global Strategic Directions for Nursing and Midwifery (SDNM).

Source: National health workforce accounts: a handbook, 2nd edition, indicator 2-03 (page 68), word for word, from the ingested L1 node in who-iris. Draft L2 indicator NHWA.2-03, for working-group review.
ind:nhwa-2-04:
Indicator. 2-04 Ratio of graduates to stock

NHWA indicator 2-04: Ratio of graduates to stock. Ratio of graduates of health workforce education and training programmes to the stock of active health workers

Numerator Denominator Disaggregation
Number of graduates from a cohort of a health workforce education and training programme Number of active health workers, defined in headcounts By health workforce education and training programme, by health workforce education and training programme and sex, by health workforce education and training programme and health education and training institution ownership (public/private)

Definition: This indicator aims to approach the graduation rate using data available on an annual basis. The exact graduation rate can also be calculated from longitudinal information on students following cohorts of students. If such data are available, the graduation rate estimated from the most recent complete cohort can be reported. In addition to the total number of graduates, distribution of graduates by sex and by ownership enables to identify potential maldistribution and inequities.

Potential data sources: Databases of health education and training institutions; Health workforce registry or database; Professional council/chamber/association registers.

Reporting: Annual. Frameworks: Global Strategy for Human Resources for Health: Workforce 2030 (GSHRH), Working for Health programme, Global Strategic Directions for Nursing and Midwifery (SDNM), SCORE for Health Data Technical Package (SCORE).

Data elements in this chapter: de:cde-sex, de:nhwa-m2-qualification, de:nhwa-m2-training-institution.

Source: National health workforce accounts: a handbook, 2nd edition, indicator 2-04 (page 69), word for word, from the ingested L1 node in who-iris. Draft L2 indicator NHWA.2-04, for working-group review.
ind:nhwa-2-05:
Indicator. 2-05 Duration of education and training

NHWA indicator 2-05: Duration of education and training. Duration of health workforce education and training programmes, in years

Numerator Denominator Disaggregation
not printed in the NHWA handbook; for the working group not printed in the NHWA handbook; for the working group By health workforce education and training programme

Definition: Duration of health workforce education and training is the number of years required to complete a full curriculum for each health workforce education and training programme. This duration does not include specializations or time to obtain additional, optional, certifications.

Potential data sources: Ministry of Education; Database on education and training statistics; Education and training institutions.

Reporting: Annual. Frameworks: Global Strategic Directions for Nursing and Midwifery (SDNM).

Source: National health workforce accounts: a handbook, 2nd edition, indicator 2-05 (page 70), word for word, from the ingested L1 node in who-iris. Draft L2 indicator NHWA.2-05, for working-group review.
ind:nhwa-2-06:
Indicator. 2-06 Accreditation mechanisms for education and training institutions and their programmes

NHWA indicator 2-06: Accreditation mechanisms for education and training institutions and their programmes. Existence of national and/or subnational mechanisms for accreditation of health workforce education and training institutions and their programmes (Yes/Partial/No)

Numerator Denominator Disaggregation
not printed in the NHWA handbook; for the working group not printed in the NHWA handbook; for the working group By health workforce education and training programme

Definition: The following questions should guide a response to this indicator: • Have national and/or subnational mechanisms for accreditation of health workforce education and training institutions and their programmes been established? • Are national and/or subnational mechanisms for accreditation of health workforce education and training institutions and their programmes compulsory? • Are there national and/or subnational mechanisms for accreditation of health workforce education and training institutions and their programmes that are not compulsory? • If established, do national and/or subnational mechanisms for accreditation of health workforce education and training institutions and their programmes take into account national education plans for the health workforce?

Potential data sources: Ministry of Health; Ministries of Education, Higher Education or similar; National accreditation authorities; Legitimate bodies, statutory corporations; Professional council/chamber/association registers.

Reporting: Every three years. Frameworks: Global Strategy for Human Resources for Health: Workforce 2030 (GSHRH), Working for Health programme, Global Strategic Directions for Nursing and Midwifery (SDNM), Primary Health Care (PHC) Measurement Framework.

Source: National health workforce accounts: a handbook, 2nd edition, indicator 2-06 (page 71), word for word, from the ingested L1 node in who-iris. Draft L2 indicator NHWA.2-06, for working-group review.
ind:nhwa-2-07:
Indicator. 2-07 Standards for education and training programmes

NHWA indicator 2-07: Standards for education and training programmes. Existence of standards for education and training programmes

Numerator Denominator Disaggregation
not printed in the NHWA handbook; for the working group not printed in the NHWA handbook; for the working group By health workforce education and training programme (for all but last sub-indicator 2-07.7)

Definition: This indicator is a composite of seven sub-indicators, see below. The response to these seven sub-indicators is aggregated as a score (see part II on methods) on a scale from 1 (nascent) to 5 (sustainable). Each sub-indicator is a self-assessment of one aspect of standards on education and training programmes. To help answer these self-assessed sub-indicators, a series of guiding questions are provided.

Sub-indicators:

  • 2-07.1 Existence of national and/or subnational standards for social accountability in accreditation mechanisms of training programmes (Yes/Partial/No)
  • 2-07.2 Existence of national and/or subnational standards for the social determinants of health in accreditation mechanisms of training programmes (Yes/Partial/No)
  • 2-07.3 Existence of national and/or subnational standards for interprofessional education in accreditation mechanisms of training programmes (Yes/Partial/No)
  • 2-07.4 Existence of cooperation between health workforce education and training institutions and regulatory bodies to agree on accreditation standards (Yes/Partial/No)
  • 2-07.5 Existence of national systems for continuing professional development (Yes/Partial/No)
  • 2-07.6 Existence of in-service training as an element of national education plans for the health workforce (Yes/Partial/No)
  • 2-07.7 Existence of national and/or subnational standards for community health workers’ curriculum (Yes/ Partial/No/Not applicable)

Potential data sources: Ministry of Health; Ministries of Education, Higher Education or similar; National accreditation authorities; Legitimate bodies, statutory corporations; Professional council/chamber/association registers; Ministries responsible for labour.

Reporting: Every three years. Frameworks: Global Strategy for Human Resources for Health: Workforce 2030 (GSHRH), Global Strategic Directions for Nursing and Midwifery (SDNM), Primary Health Care (PHC) Measurement Framework, Community Health Workers (CHWs).

Source: National health workforce accounts: a handbook, 2nd edition, indicator 2-07 (pages 72-73), word for word, from the ingested L1 node in who-iris. Draft L2 indicator NHWA.2-07, for working-group review.

prose:ch11-nhwa-m3:
• Extension data elements a registry can hold to support NHWA Module 3 (finance and expenditures). They are optional.
  • The module's indicators are mostly expenditure totals from finance and health ministry records, not registry data.

ind:nhwa-3-01:
Indicator. 3-01 Expenditure on compensation of health workers

NHWA indicator 3-01: Expenditure on compensation of health workers. Total expenditure on compensation of health workers

Numerator Denominator Disaggregation
not printed in the NHWA handbook; for the working group not printed in the NHWA handbook; for the working group By public/private

Definition: Total expenditure expressed in US$ on compensation of health workers. If possible, disaggregation by public or private sources for the compensation of health workers. Sometimes information is only available for public expenditure on compensation of health workers.

Potential data sources: Ministry of Health records; Ministry of Finance records; Public/social health insurance; System of health accounts.

ind:nhwa-3-02:
Indicator. 3-02 Entry-level wages and salaries

NHWA indicator 3-02: Entry-level wages and salaries. Average entry-level wage and salary excluding social contributions

Numerator Denominator Disaggregation
not printed in the NHWA handbook; for the working group not printed in the NHWA handbook; for the working group By occupation, by occupation and public/private

Definition: Average wage or salary in US$ received by health workers when entering the active health labour market, excluding social contributions. Disaggregation by public vs private source is suggested, although often only the source from the public sector is available.

Potential data sources: Ministry of Health records; Ministry of Finance records; Payroll data; Income tax data; General labour force surveys; Specific health worker surveys.

Reporting: Annual. Frameworks: Global Strategic Directions for Nursing and Midwifery (SDNM).

ind:nhwa-3-03:
Indicator. 3-03 Total expenditure on health workforce education

NHWA indicator 3-03: Total expenditure on health workforce education. Total expenditure on health workforce pre-service education (current and capital)

Numerator Denominator Disaggregation
not printed in the NHWA handbook; for the working group not printed in the NHWA handbook; for the working group By health workforce education and training programme, by health workforce education and training programme and institution ownership (public/private)

Definition: Total expenditure in US$ on health workforce education (current and capital). The disaggregation enables to differentiate between public vs private sources and distribution across programmes. Education here refers to pre-service education and does not include in-service education and training.

Potential data sources: Integrated Financial Management Information System; Ministry of Finance; Ministry of Health; Ministry of Education; Ministry of Defence (expenditure on military HWF education may fall under the Ministry of Defence budget); Education Management Information System: Ministry of (Higher) Education; ministry or other accredited bodies responsible for technical and vocational education and training; National Bureau of Statistics – Government financial statistics departments; System of Health Accounts; National Education Accounts.

Reporting: Annual. Frameworks: Global Strategic Directions for Nursing and Midwifery (SDNM).

Source: National health workforce accounts: a handbook, 2nd edition, indicator 3-03 (page 78), word for word, from the ingested L1 node in who-iris. Draft L2 indicator NHWA.3-03, for working-group review.
ind:nhwa-3-04:
Indicator. 3-04 Expenditure per graduate on health workforce education

NHWA indicator 3-04: Expenditure per graduate on health workforce education. Expenditure per graduate of health workforce education and training programme

Numerator Denominator Disaggregation
Total expenditure on health workforce education Total number of graduates from health workforce education and training programmes By health workforce education and training programme, by health workforce education and training programme and institution ownership (public/private)

Definition: Expenditure in US$ on health workforce education per graduate. The disaggregation by programme enables to identify inequities across programmes. The disaggregation by institution ownership enables to distinguish between publicly and privately owned education institutions.

Potential data sources: Integrated Financial Management Information System: Ministry of Finance; Ministry of Health; Ministry of Education; Ministry of Defence (expenditure on military HWF education may fall under this budget); Education Management Information System: Ministry of (Higher) Education; ministry or other accredited body responsible for technical and vocational education and training; National Bureau of Statistics – Government financial statistics departments; System of Health Accounts; National Education Accounts.

Numerator Denominator Disaggregation
Total tuition fees paid by students enrolled in health workforce education and training programmes for a given year Total number of students enrolled in health workforce education and training programmes By health workforce education and training programme

Definition: Average tuition fee in US$ per student enrolled in health workforce education and training per year, by health workforce education and training programme. Whenever possible, this indicator should exclude students exonerated from paying tuition fees.
